# Independent proactive visual QA — issue #80

Reviewed issue: [Sign in and restore a protected session without replaying work](https://github.com/dystrophyless/dubbed.ai/issues/80). Reviewer: **GPT-6.1 Sol / High**, dedicated solely to #80. Date: **2026-10-25 Asia/Qyzylorda** (capture timestamps use UTC, beginning 2026-10-24). Review only; no product, specification, GitHub, commit or push changes.

## Verdict and boundary

**Three MEDIUM findings: two confirmed implementation defects and one requirement/design flaw. No HIGH or LOW findings.** The ordinary mock sign-in and Account reauthentication destinations work. The main concerns are actionable recovery and the compact desktop authentication controls. This is a bounded review, not renewed acceptance of all checked issue criteria.

Code HEAD is `9d286621177200fdb5f61ef963d0b6818ae76774`. `git diff --name-only -- frontend` was empty. The repository already contained extensive dirty documentation, skills and historical evidence; [worktree-boundary.txt](worktree-boundary.txt) records the boundary. Only this issue-80 directory was written. Current issue snapshot: [contracts/issue-80.md](../contracts/issue-80.md), fetched by the coordinator on 2026-10-25, closed with zero comments. Current local Flow 02/shared/token/adoption documents were used, including the settled Account expiry destination of **New dub**. Some flow file headers still describe their specification-only historical phase; executed browser evidence here describes the present mock app.

User job: enter a trusted account session, understand and recover from authentication failures, and resume a permitted persisted destination without repeating the interrupted command. Sign-in itself must not create/upload/process/purchase/record anything.

## Method and provenance

Used Ponytail full, spec-task-review, frontend-design and design-taste-frontend/app-screen guidance; the selected Affect UI contract takes precedence over generic aesthetic direction. Read repository HANDOFF, SDD entry point, applicable flow and live issue snapshot. Source discovery used Semble, then direct reads.

Started `npm.cmd run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4380 --strictPort` from `D:/Program/python/Dubbed/frontend`; package dev is `vite --mode mock`. Used installed Playwright Chromium, isolated contexts, DPR 1, muted audio and fake-device/fake-UI flags. Default Windows sandbox initialization failed; bounded escalated shell calls ran the authorized read/capture work. No real credentials, provider, email, microphone, backend or deployed app was used.

Commands: `node .../issue-80/capture.cjs`, `node .../issue-80/session.cjs`, `node .../issue-80/targeted.cjs`. See [capture script](capture.cjs), [session script](session.cjs), [targeted check](targeted.cjs), [raw DOM metrics](metrics.json), [capture log](capture-log.json), [session assertions](session-check.json), [duplicate-submit result/browser version](targeted-check.json), and [screenshot manifest](screenshot-manifest.json). Screenshots are full-page captures; their viewport dimensions and fold positions are recorded separately. Every PNG in the manifest was opened with `view_image` and inspected.

Primary forms and credentials errors use the actual application UI. Pending, unavailable confirmation, unavailable adapter and provider conflict use the existing `e2e/harness/auth-state-visual.html` with its explicit scenario handlers. These exercise real components against synthetic service responses, not a live provider. The held pending service received exactly one `identity.signIn` call after initial submit, a forced second click and Enter; `aria-busy=true`, `aria-disabled=true`, native disabled=false were recorded. This check ran with reduced motion; no complete motion timing audit is claimed.

For the success/expiry journey only, direct mock registration.start/verify/signOut created a disposable synthetic account in the isolated context. Sign-in was then performed through UI. One IndexedDB mock session's expiresAt was moved into the past, followed by reload. This is an injected expiry observation, not a 30-day wall-clock test. The pre-expiry session expiry remained identical across reload, approximately 2,592,000,000ms from sign-in. An initial capture attempt incorrectly assumed expiry auto-redirected to sign-in and timed out; the final script explicitly captures the actual expiry gate and tests its Retry action.

## Expected versus actual

| AC / state | Expected contract | Fresh observed result | Evidence / assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC-01 empty/invalid fields | Field messages below fields, bilingual, values retained for active-form failure | EN/RU validation appears immediately below outlined fields; actual invalid credentials uses exact neutral English copy above primary; email/password retained | `en-phone-validation`, `ru-phone-validation`, `en-desktop-invalid-credentials`; covered subset |
| AC-01 pending | Stable status, duplicate guard | Primary retains readable color and changes to Signing in; duplicate password service call suppressed | `signin-loading`, targeted-check.json; pass for held mock |
| AC-02 provider conflict | Method-owned-elsewhere conflict explained without merging; safe recovery | Generic stale-data message instead of identity conflict explanation | `signin-provider-conflict`; QA-80-02 |

## Findings

### QA-80-01 — MEDIUM — Expired session offers a Retry loop instead of contextual reauthentication

**Class:** confirmed implementation defect in recovery UX; confirmed observation, no private-data leak. **Affected:** AC-03/04, Flow02 section6 and Account expiry handoff.

**Reproduce:** seed the disposable mock account as documented, UI sign-in, open Account, set its mock session expiresAt before now and reload. Activate the only action in the content region, Retry.

**Expected:** explain that the session ended and give a direct, correctly labelled Sign in continuation. A stable expired session is distinct from an unavailable lookup that can recover by repeating the read. After authentication, retain the already confirmed New dub destination for Account.

**Actual:** the Account body is correctly removed, but says **“This request expired. Start again.”** and offers **Retry**. Clicking Retry leaves the same URL and exact message/action. The header's small Sign in link works, but the dominant recovery action does not resolve the condition or explain that route. session-check.json records expiredAccountText and expiredRetryText equality, both at `/account`.

![Expired session gate](D:/Program/python/Dubbed/_docs/evidence/proactive-visual-qa-2026-10-25/issue-80/evidence/en-account-expiry-gate.png)
![After Retry](D:/Program/python/Dubbed/_docs/evidence/proactive-visual-qa-2026-10-25/issue-80/evidence/en-account-expiry-retry.png)

**Cause evidence:** [App.tsx:74](D:/Program/python/Dubbed/frontend/src/App.tsx:74) maps identity error codes into the generic error state; [FeatureRoute.tsx:109](D:/Program/python/Dubbed/frontend/src/app/FeatureRoute.tsx:109) supplies the same refreshIdentity Retry for every error; [messages.ts:53](D:/Program/python/Dubbed/frontend/src/i18n/messages.ts:53) uses request-expiry language. This is broader than Account's own screen because the protected gate renders first.

**Impact:** a returning user can repeatedly choose the apparent recovery without reaching authentication. The working header escape makes this bounded rather than a complete sign-in outage.

**Recommendation:** distinguish authoritative expired/unauthenticated session from unavailable/unknown lookup. Provide session-specific EN/RU copy and a nearby Sign in CTA using the existing safe intent resolver; retain Retry for genuinely retryable resolution failures. **Next validation:** expire on Account and one project screen in EN/RU, activate the content CTA with keyboard and pointer, assert Account goes New dub, valid project goes its same persisted screen, and no protected mutation is repeated.

### QA-80-02 — MEDIUM — Google account conflict is rendered as stale information

**Class:** confirmed implementation mismatch. **Affected:** AC-02, AC-VIS-01 provider-return conflict; Flow02 section5.3; Flow05 owns the actual conflict/recovery continuation.

**Reproduce:** open the existing auth-state visual harness with `screen=signin&scenario=signin-provider-conflict` in RU; select Continue with Google. The captured call log records `identity.google.sign-in` once.

**Expected:** accurately explain that this Google method is associated with another account, preserve separate accounts, and offer an appropriate existing sign-in/recovery handoff without pretending that refresh can repair method ownership. The reviewed contract specifically distinguishes this outcome from a revision race.

**Actual:** **“Данные изменились. Обновите их и попробуйте снова.”** (“This information changed. Refresh and try again.”). There is no identity-conflict explanation or contextual continuation; the generic sign-in form remains. This is a synthetic authoritative conflict response, not a claim that a real Google identity was tested.

![Google conflict](D:/Program/python/Dubbed/_docs/evidence/proactive-visual-qa-2026-10-25/issue-80/evidence/signin-provider-conflict.png)

**Cause:** [SignInScreen.tsx:184](D:/Program/python/Dubbed/frontend/src/features/auth/SignInScreen.tsx:184) handles canceled/denied/link-required/account-not-found separately, then maps the remaining conflict to `setServiceError('conflict')` at188. [messages.ts:52](D:/Program/python/Dubbed/frontend/src/i18n/messages.ts:52) /147 supplies stale-data copy. The harness produces `state:'conflict'` at [auth-state-visual.tsx:181](D:/Program/python/Dubbed/frontend/e2e/harness/auth-state-visual.tsx:181).

**Impact:** users cannot tell which account/method problem needs resolution and are encouraged to repeat an unrelated remedy. No merge or data-loss defect is asserted.

**Recommendation:** add a localized provider-conflict presentation and reuse the approved Flow05 recovery entry. Keep account identifiers/private facts within the authorized disclosure contract. **Next validation:** EN/RU desktop/phone conflict, cancellation and link-required side by side; assert distinct copy and destinations and unchanged account/balance/grant history.

### QA-80-03 — MEDIUM — Compact desktop density is a poor fit for the primary authentication task

**Class:** requirement/design flaw, not a claim that following the approved button dimensions violates accessibility. **Affected:** AC-06 / VIS; tokens section4 and Flow02 authentication hierarchy.

**Measured facts:** at1440px the Sign in and Google targets are **350×28px**, with **13px/20px** Mabry Medium text; password visibility is **350×24px**, **12px/16px**. Inputs are350×40px with16px/24px text. At390px all three actions are48px high with16px/24px text. At767/768 the primary drops48→28px in one CSS pixel. The 400px desktop panel is surrounded by ample empty space, so a dense data-table rationale does not apply. The checkbox-free, two-field authentication form is the essential entry task.

![Desktop authentication hierarchy](D:/Program/python/Dubbed/_docs/evidence/proactive-visual-qa-2026-10-25/issue-80/evidence/en-desktop-empty.png)
![At 768px](D:/Program/python/Dubbed/_docs/evidence/proactive-visual-qa-2026-10-25/issue-80/evidence/ru-boundary-768.png)

**Interpretation:** the dark primary is distinguishable, but its thin strip and small label make the frequent, consequential entry action unnecessarily delicate compared with the field text and large recovery links. The24px/12px helper label is particularly small. Wide targets reduce horizontal acquisition difficulty but do not compensate for the vertical hit area or small text. These dimensions alone do not establish a WCAG failure; the critique concerns product hierarchy, readability and comfort.

**Contract/source:** [design-tokens.md:86](D:/Program/python/Dubbed/_docs/frontend-flows/design-tokens.md:86) explicitly adopts24/28/32px compact desktop controls. BTN Clean CSS289–376 sets28px/13px medium,24px/12px small,6px radius; its initial/loading Light PNGs were opened. The actual dark primary, white secondary,6px radii and visible accent focus preserve the selected language. The problem is applying compact component-demo density to this particular job.

**Recommendation:** record a narrowly scoped authentication exception: primary/provider targets around40–44px and labels14–16px, with a readable password visibility action; retain Mabry, colors,6px radius, source shadow and focus. Do not globally enlarge all product controls. **Next validation:** compare current/proposed EN/RU forms at768 and1440, including short700px windows, error/pending states and keyboard focus; confirm readable hierarchy and no new overflow.

## What works and visual comparison

Both languages retain clear field labels, readable input values, distinct dark submit and blue recovery links.
